headline: Record revenue and profit as Data Center demand surges
summary_short: AMD reported record Q2 revenue of $11.5B (+50% y/y), driven by Data Center revenue more than doubling to $6.7B, with diluted EPS of $1.38 (+156% y/y) and operating income swinging to $2.0B from a year-ago loss.
summary_long: Revenue reached a record $11.5B (+50% y/y, +13% q/q), led by Data Center revenue of $6.7B (+107% y/y, 58% of total), as EPYC and Instinct GPU demand accelerated. GAAP gross margin rose to 54% (+14ppt y/y) as the year-ago quarter absorbed an $800M MI308 export-control inventory charge; non-GAAP gross margin was 56%. Operating income swung to $2.0B from a $134M loss a year earlier; diluted EPS reached $1.38 (+156% y/y). Cash and short-term investments totaled $13.1B. AMD guided Q3 2026 revenue to approximately $13B ±$300M (~41% y/y growth at midpoint) with non-GAAP gross margin near 56%, citing accelerating Data Center demand into H2.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited a record quarter as Data Center revenue more than doubled year-over-year, with EPYC demand accelerating, Instinct deployments scaling and Helios beginning to ramp.
Growth was led by Data Center (+107% y/y, 58% of revenue) on EPYC and Instinct demand, plus Client +23% on Ryzen demand, partly offset by Gaming -31% on lower semi-custom revenue.
Y/y margin comparison benefits from a depressed year-ago base: Q2'25 GAAP results included an $800M inventory-related charge tied to the U.S. government's MI308 export-control action.
The swing from a $134M operating loss to $2.0B of operating income reflects the same $800M MI308 export-control inventory charge that depressed Q2'25, plus revenue growth.
Beyond the operating-income swing, the filing's own non-GAAP reconciliation table attributes $483M of the period's $598M other income to gains on long-term investments.
